Gentlemen Prefer Blondes (1953) is one of Hollywood’s most iconic musical comedies, starring Marilyn Monroe and Jane Russell. Monroe plays Lorelei Lee, a glamorous showgirl traveling to France to marry her wealthy fiancé, while Russell’s sharp-witted Dorothy Shaw joins her for a journey filled with romance, mistaken identities, and plenty of chaos. The film playfully satirizes materialism and gender stereotypes, but it’s Monroe’s unforgettable performance of “Diamonds Are a Girl’s Best Friend” that made it a true classic.

Marilyn Monroe reportedly came up with the line, “I can be smart when it’s important, but most men don’t like it,” which perfectly captures Lorelei’s charm and wit. Behind the scenes, the studio originally wanted to dub all of Monroe’s singing because they felt her voice sounded too unusual. Singer Marni Nixon strongly opposed the idea, believing Monroe’s voice was an essential part of her screen presence. In the end, Nixon only sang the operatic “no, no, nos” at the beginning of “Diamonds Are a Girl’s Best Friend” and the line, “these rocks don’t lose their shape,” leaving the rest of the performance entirely Monroe’s own.
